title: PostgreSQL Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this PostgreSQL course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: What does AS total_books do?
questions.explanation: A SELECT query can calculate a value without reading a table. An alias gives the answer column a clear name.

questions.question: Which rule requires a title?
questions.explanation: A table names the facts each row can hold. An identity column can create a new numeric id automatically.

questions.question: What does RETURNING show?
options: Values from the row just inserted
questions.explanation: RETURNING asks PostgreSQL to show values from a row it has just changed. It is useful for reading an automatically made id.

questions.question: What does the percent sign match?
questions.explanation: ILIKE is PostgreSQL's case-insensitive pattern match. A percent sign matches any length of text.

questions.question: Why sort before LIMIT?
options: To make the chosen first rows meaningful
To make all rows have the same page count
questions.explanation: ORDER BY chooses the result order. LIMIT then restricts how many of those rows are returned.

questions.question: What does count(*) count?
options: Only letters in the group name
questions.explanation: GROUP BY puts matching values together. An aggregate such as count gives one answer for each group.

questions.question: What links the two records?
options: Their row positions happen to match
questions.explanation: A join matches rows using a shared value. It can put an author name beside a book title stored in another table.

questions.question: Why is the final count zero?
questions.explanation: A transaction groups changes into one job. ROLLBACK cancels uncommitted changes so you can practise safely with sample data.

questions.question: What does ->> return for a JSON field?
questions.explanation: JSONB stores JSON data in a form PostgreSQL can query. The ->> operator reads one field as text.

questions.question: Why is allowed true?
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL can store an array of values. ANY can test whether a value matches one item in that array.

questions.question: Does row_number merge the rows into one group result?
options: Yes, it removes every original row
questions.explanation: A window function calculates across related rows while keeping each row visible. row_number can number a sorted result.

questions.question: What does plain EXPLAIN do?
options: Guarantees that an index is always fastest
Shows the planned work without executing this SELECT for results
questions.explanation: EXPLAIN shows how PostgreSQL plans to run a query. It can help you understand a table scan before guessing which index to add.
